question:
An engineer is duplicating an existing Cisco UCS setup at a new site.
What are two characteristics of a logical configuration backup of a Cisco UCS Manager database? (Choose two.)
options: contains the configured organizations and locales
contains the VLAN and VSAN configurations
contains the AAA and RBAC configurations
contains a file with an extension .tgz that stores all of the configurations
theory: A Logical Configuration backup is an XML export of logical objects only — organizations/locales together with service profiles and their related VLAN/VSAN, pool, and policy definitions — which makes it suitable for duplicating a UCS setup's logical layout at a new site. It does not include the AAA/RBAC (system configuration) settings, nor is it the .tgz-style complete binary dump that a Full State backup produces; those distinctions (what's XML vs binary, and what object classes are covered) are exactly what separates the four Cisco UCS Manager backup types. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 14 — UCS Configuration Management, Backup Types)
